claims.statement: tests/ is primarily a read-only fixture corpus (30 Logiqx DAT files plus the ROM, disc-image, archive, patch and header files they declare) consumed by the src/<module>/test_*.rs modules, and only tests/crates.rs and tests/mcp_stdio.rs are actual integration-test targets of the root package. crates/chd-rs/tests/ additionally reads the repository's CHD fixtures from ../../tests as its byte-comparison corpus.

Because importing relocates a romfile (rename_file, with copy+remove only as the cross-filesystem fallback), tests must copy a fixture into a scratch directory and import the copy; only read-not-imported fixtures (.ird, profile.xml, DAT zips, the DATs themselves) are referenced directly in tests/.

Test scratch directories are created inside tests/ with TempDir::new_in(test_directory), keeping fixtures and their imported results on one filesystem so the rename path is exercised; .gitignore lists tests/.tmp* for the leftovers.

Fixture DATs are named 'Test System (<YYYYMMDD>)[ (<Scenario>)].dat', but the file name is only a lookup string: database identity comes from <header><name>, matched by find_system_by_name, so a scenario DAT that must update the same system keeps <name>Test System</name> and carries the suffix only in the file name (including both Test System (20240626) (Multiple Orphan Roms*) DATs), while a scenario DAT that is its own system repeats the suffix in <name>.

is_update compares DAT version strings lexicographically: a lower or equal version skips the import entirely and only a greater one updates the system (bypassable with --force), which is why the deliberately ancient Test System (20000000).dat exists to prove an older catalog changes nothing.

A DAT's file-name date and <version> may deliberately disagree: Test System (20240908) (Patches).dat carries version 20230112 and header name 'Test System (Parent-Clone) (Revisions)', and Test System (20241230) (MAME Mixed).dat reuses both the header name and version of Test System (20241228) (MAME CHD).dat, so its test asserts the MAME CHD system name.

Each DAT <rom> row is a checksum contract with a file in tests/: the name must match byte for byte (including double extensions and '(Track 01)' spacing) and size plus one hash must match the bytes, since matching uses CRC first, then MD5, then SHA1, and fails with 'Size mismatch' or 'Checksum mismatch'.

For containers the DAT declares the entries inside, not the container: archives and CHDs are matched against rom rows naming their inner .rom/.cue/.bin files, so one catalog drives every packaging format under test.

MAME arcade DAT fixtures' <disk> rows carry only a SHA1 and no size, matching MAME's own CHD DATs; import_chd has a dedicated retry that looks the file up by chd_sha1 with size 0 on every non-CD branch - DVD, HD and LaserDisc - and an arcade system stores the matched CHD under <system>/<game>/.

Checksums for new fixtures are produced by tests/compute_sums.sh, which prints per file the ls -l size, the CRC via rhash -C --simple, the MD5 and the SHA1 - exactly the four fields a DAT <rom> row needs; regenerating a fixture therefore invalidates the DAT rows that describe it.

tests/header.xml is a clrmamepro header-detector fixture (NES magic at offset 10) referenced by <clrmamepro header="header.xml" /> in the Headered DATs; import resolves it next to the DAT first and falls back to the embedded data/ assets, and parse_dat's skip_header flag suppresses it entirely.

Network-facing fixtures are replayed through wiremock: tests/profile.xml answers GET /profile.xml for the no-intro DAT flow and Test System (20200721).zip is the redump datfile payload a mocked GET /datfile/<CODE> returns, while Test System (20210401).zip supplies a DAT nested in a subdirectory for import-dats.

Patch fixtures form a known-answer triple: the committed .ips/.bps/.xdelta patches applied to Test Game (USA, Europe).rom must reproduce the committed Test Game (USA, Europe) (patched).rom byte for byte.

tests/crates.rs is a workspace-level parity guard, not a behaviour test: its every_cli_shares_one_ui reads crates/xso-rs/src/bin/xsors/ui.rs and asserts the copies in chdrs, ciars, gdirs, nszrs, wuxrs, xdeltars and xpsrs are byte-identical, so changing one CLI shell without the other seven fails with "<path> differs from xsors's ui.rs" and all eight must always be edited together.

The MCP stdio harness spawns the real binary via CARGO_BIN_EXE_oxyromon with `mcp`, isolates it with OXYROMON_DATA_DIRECTORY pointing at a TempDir held by the Client (so a virgin oxyromon.db is created per test) and OXYROMON_LOG_LEVEL=off with stderr nulled, and speaks raw newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout with no SDK client - which is also what proves the wire format a real client would meet.

The harness reads responses one line at a time and returns only the one whose id matches the request, discarding anything else, so server-initiated notifications can interleave with a call without desynchronising the test; a non-JSON line on stdout aborts the test, which is the automated guard on 'stdout carries nothing but protocol messages'.

close() drops the child's stdin and asserts the process exits with success status: stdin EOF must terminate the MCP server cleanly, the observable half of the tokio::select! on server.waiting() in mcp::main.

The stdio suite pins the advertised surface: initialize reports serverInfo.name oxyromon, tools/list contains all 20 tools, prompts/list is exactly [audit_system, onboard_system] and resources/list is exactly [oxyromon://status, oxyromon://systems, oxyromon://settings] in that order.

Over stdio the suite pins three behaviour contracts: status reports CARGO_PKG_VERSION with read_only false and 0 systems on the empty library; an unknown system id is a tool-level isError whose text points at list_systems; and importing tests/Test System (20200721).dat through import_dats yields one system with games_total 6 and matching search/list counts.

Destructive tools are confirm-gated and setting validation is shared with the CLI: purge_roms and purge_games with confirm omitted and purge_systems/purge_irds with confirm:false return isError text naming confirm, and set_setting accepts PREFER_REGIONS=broad, rejects 'mars' with 'valid' and rejects unknown keys, with the accepted value readable back through get_settings.

With --read-only the mutating tools are both absent from tools/list and refused at the protocol layer (a JSON-RPC error object, not an isError tool result), the distinction produced by disabling the write router's routes rather than by a tool-level denial.

tests/mcp_stdio.rs is #![cfg(feature = "mcp")] so without that feature it contributes no tests; server implies mcp, so CI's single cargo llvm-cov --workspace --features oxyromon/server step runs it, and the MCP-without-web-server combination is covered separately by cargo clippy --no-default-features --features use-rustls,mcp --all-targets.

CHD fixtures are consumed in process by src/chd.rs on top of crates/chd-rs: parse_chd reads ChdType, logical size, data SHA1, file SHA1, parent SHA1 and track_count from the container, and import/check/convert/export all run without any external binary (chd::get_version returns "built-in"); there is no src/chdman.rs fixture helper and nothing in src/ spawns chdman.

Each committed CHD fixture exercises one ChdType branch of the importer: (Multiple Tracks).chd is a Cd whose every extracted track must hash against the DAT's .cue + (Track 0n).bin rows before the CHD is accepted, (Single Track).chd takes the unsplit track_count == 1 path, (ISO).chd is a Dvd whose extracted image is hashed by ChdRomfile::get_hash_and_size, and (RDSK).chd is an Hd matched through the CHD-SHA1 retry.

Test Game (USA, Europe) (LD).riff is the workspace's only LaserDisc fixture and is consumed solely by src/chd/test_ld.rs, which asserts .riff -> to_chd -> as_chd -> to_riff -> to_chd yields a byte-identical CHD; crates/chd-rs/tests/cli.rs deliberately excludes the LaserDisc-flavoured (RDSK) fixture from its chdman comparison because the avhu codec has no oracle there.

Three tests/ CHD fixtures are reused across crate boundaries: crates/chd-rs/tests/cli.rs opens them through ../../tests and pins chdrs info for the DVD fixture to a golden report (SHA1 7c6c71c6..., Data SHA1 762a227d...), so regenerating a committed CHD invalidates that golden text as well as the DAT rows in tests/.

The DAT-update orphan fixtures pair a second import_dat with an explicit romfile count and trash verdict, and the two DATs disagree on purpose: after importing (Multiple Tracks).cue + .chd, the renamed (Multiple Orphan Roms).dat leaves 3 roms / 2 romfiles with nothing trashed while the (Multiple Orphan Roms Mismatch).dat trashes one, and the same pair over Test Game (USA, Europe) (Full).7z yields 1 romfile either way with the mismatch variant trashing it and clearing every romfile_id.

Trash assertions across the suite are substring checks (romfile.path.contains("/Trash/")) because the trash directory is per-system (<system>/Trash) or global (<ROM directory>/Trash); get_trash_directory owns that choice.

The shared fixture-test setup skeleton is a test-only API: config.rs declares MUTEX, set_rom_directory and set_tmp_directory inside cfg_if!/cfg(test) blocks, so no production build can register a scratch ROM or tmp directory.

The MCP stdio harness is the only fixture-consuming suite that does not create its scratch TempDir inside tests/: its isolated data directory comes from TempDir::new() in the system temp directory, held by the Client struct, while import-asserting tests use TempDir::new_in(test_directory).

import-dats accepts DAT archives as well as loose .dat files: it partitions arguments by .zip extension, extracts each archive into the tmp directory and walks the tree for .dat files including subdirectories, which is what tests/Test System (20210401).zip (a DAT under Test System/) exercises.
The stdio suite pins the convert_roms format gate end to end: after importing the test DAT, a lowercase "zip" is accepted and "nkit" is refused with "unknown format".
crates/cia-rs/tests/data/Test Game (USA, Europe).cia is a byte-identical copy of tests/Test Game (USA, Europe).cia, so the published cia-rs crate carries its own known-answer fixture.

The merged-layout tests share `src/rebuild_roms/merged_set.rs`, which builds split ZIPs from the MAME Merged DAT at run time, a parent plus two clones covering a name clash and a file shared by sibling clones, and asserts the merged layout and a clean `check-roms` run.

The Wii U fixtures are synthetic: tests/Test Game (USA).wud (1867776 bytes, with an update partition) and its .wux are declared by Test System (20261025) (WUD).dat as Test Game (USA).iso, the update folder tests/Test Game (USA) (Update)/ holds tmd.48, cetk.48 and contents 00000010 to 00000012 with 00000012.h3 under No-Intro's CDN names for Test System (20261025) (CDN).dat, and tests/Test Game (USA).keys.txt holds made-up keys that src/wux.rs reads under cfg(test).
export_roms/test_wux_with_ticketless_update_to_wua.rs imports the WUD and CDN DATs, removes the update's cetk.48, and asserts the WUA holds the game's folder but not the update's.
